verdict.paragraph: Bakon scores 52 out of 100, a wide gap from where a category leader should sit. Rademaker scores 69 and pulls ahead most sharply on brand identity, setting a visible benchmark for what buyers expect from a serious bakery equipment supplier. The machinery is real and the offer is clear, but aging design, a broken mobile widget, no video, and thin proof points are costing credibility across every category. Product visuals is the first place to fix.

firstFix.why: Product visuals score 8 out of 20, the lowest category on the scorecard. Buyers evaluating depositing and cutting equipment want to see machines running before they request a quote. Without video, a buyer comparing Bakon against Unifiller or Rademaker will find motion content on competitor sites and nothing equivalent here. That gap costs consideration before a conversation even starts.
firstFix.inPractice: Film two or three machines running at production speed, each clip between 60 and 90 seconds, showing product going in and coming out. Place one clip on the homepage hero and one on each relevant product page. A short voiceover or on-screen text naming the output rate and product type gives buyers the proof point they are looking for. Static photography stays, but video becomes the lead asset.
